description: A junior Computer Science major with a specialization in Cybersecurity and professional experience in firmware development who seeks to understand OS internals for security auditing.

nodes.title: Classic OS Foundations & System Structures
nodes.personalizationRationale: As a student with strong_prior_exposure, you will start with this core floor node to align your existing knowledge with the course's specific structural definitions.
nodes.description: An overview of OS services, structures, and the kernel/user mode distinction fundamental to all systems programming.

nodes.title: Architectural Analysis of System Interfaces
nodes.description: In-depth analysis of system calls and interrupt handling mechanisms with a focus on hardware-software interface performance.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Leveraging your strong_prior_exposure, this enrichment node replaces introductory scaffolding with a deeper look at kernel-mode transition overhead.

nodes.title: Process Lifecycle & Management
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node ensures that even with your strong_prior_exposure, the specific process state models used for exam evaluation are mastered.
nodes.description: Exploration of the process abstraction, lifecycle management, and the mechanics of context switching.

nodes.title: Advanced Inter-Process Communication Tradeoffs
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since you have strong_prior_exposure, we move past basic IPC definitions to evaluate the scalability tradeoffs of different communication primitives.
nodes.description: Comparative study of shared memory versus message passing, focusing on cache coherency and synchronization overhead.
Introduction to multithreading models and the POSIX threads library used in upcoming projects.
nodes.personalizationRationale: While you likely have strong_prior_exposure to threads, this node confirms your proficiency with the specific threading libraries required for course deliverables.
nodes.title: Threading Models & Programming Libraries
CPU Scheduling Algorithms & Evaluation
nodes.description: Detailed analysis of scheduling criteria and algorithms like Round Robin, Priority, and Multi-level Queue scheduling.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core content is heavily tested on the midterm; your strong_prior_exposure allows for a focus on the analytical modeling of these algorithms.

nodes.description: Comprehensive exam covering Operating System foundations, processes, and CPU scheduling (Chapters 1-5).
nodes.personalizationRationale: This required assessment validates your understanding of foundational material before proceeding to advanced synchronization, reflecting your strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.title: Midterm Review & Assessment (Ch. 1-5)

nodes.personalizationRationale: For a student with strong_prior_exposure, this core block provides the formal theory behind the synchronization primitives you may have used in practice.
nodes.description: Addressing the critical section problem using mutex locks, semaphores, and high-level monitors.
nodes.title: Synchronization Primitives & Monitors
Advanced Problems in Process Synchronization
nodes.description: Analysis of complex synchronization scenarios, including lock-free programming concepts and the Dining Philosophers optimization.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given your strong_prior_exposure, we dive into edge cases and performance optimizations for classic synchronization problems.
This block is essential for the final exam; your strong_prior_exposure helps you move efficiently through the characterization of deadlock states.
nodes.description: The four necessary conditions for deadlock and strategies for prevention and detection.
nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization & Prevention
Deadlock Avoidance & Banker's Algorithm
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node focuses on the algorithmic avoidance of deadlocks, which your strong_prior_exposure will help you grasp analytically.
nodes.description: Implementation and analysis of the Banker's algorithm for deadlock avoidance in multi-resource systems.

nodes.title: Paging & Main Memory Management
nodes.personalizationRationale: Memory management is a key project area; this core node aligns your strong_prior_exposure with the course's paging implementation requirements.
nodes.description: Examination of paging, segmentation, and address translation in modern memory management units.

nodes.title: Virtual Memory Performance & Page Replacement
nodes.personalizationRationale: Leveraging your strong_prior_exposure, we analyze the performance impact of page replacement strategies on high-load systems.
nodes.description: Investigation of thrashing, demand paging, and advanced page replacement algorithms like WSClock or LRU-approximations.

nodes.title: I/O Subsystems & File Storage Implementation
nodes.personalizationRationale: This core capstone content covers I/O performance, which builds on the systems concepts where you have strong_prior_exposure.
nodes.description: Techniques for I/O scheduling, buffering, and the implementation of file systems on physical storage.

nodes.title: High-Performance & Distributed File Systems
nodes.description: Exploration of log-structured file systems and distributed storage concepts for high-availability environments.
nodes.personalizationRationale: With your strong_prior_exposure, this node explores modern storage challenges beyond standard local file system implementations.

nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review & Assessment
nodes.description: A cumulative final review and assessment covering the full syllabus from foundations to file systems.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The final cumulative review ensures your strong_prior_exposure is synthesized across all seven course blocks for the final exam.
